literal: Without equity, if one covets the good wealth of others, their family perishing, guilt also then and there it will bring.
translation: If a person, abandoning equity, covets the valuable wealth of others, it will ruin their family and bring instant guilt upon them.
modern: நடுவுநிலைமை இல்லாமல், பிறருடைய நல்ல பொருளைக் கவர விரும்பினால், அவனுடைய குடும்பம் அழிந்து, அவனுக்குப் பழியும் உடனே வந்து சேரும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against the destructive consequences of covetousness. When a person acts without fairness (நடுவின்றி) and desires the rightfully earned, valuable wealth of another (நன்பொருள்), they bring ruin upon themselves. The poet states that such greed leads to two immediate disasters: the destruction of one's own family lineage (குடிபொன்றி) and the instant acquisition of guilt and blame (குற்றமும் ஆங்கே தரும்). Thus, coveting others' property destroys both one's social standing and moral character.
